text: SBV proposes temporary foreign currency accounts to unblock capital flows at VIFC

HÀ NỘI - The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has proposed allowing businesses operating at the Việt Nam International Financial Centre (VIFC) to temporarily hold capital and foreign currency payment accounts at banks outside the centre, as no member bank has yet been licensed to operate there.

The proposal, raised in a draft decree amending Decree 329/2025/NĐ-CP issued on December 18, 2025 on banking licences, foreign exchange management and anti-money laundering at VIFC, aims to ensure uninterrupted capital flows from overseas investors into the centre while its banking infrastructure is being established.
Under the draft, member businesses would be allowed to open temporary capital accounts at commercial banks or foreign bank branches operating in Việt Nam but outside the VIFC.

Once a member bank receives its licence and begins providing account services, businesses would have 60 days to transfer their balances to capital accounts opened at the VIFC and close their temporary accounts.
The draft also allows each member business to maintain a temporary foreign currency payment account at a commercial bank or foreign bank branch outside the centre.
The move is intended to facilitate overseas capital transfers, including contributions to establish IFC members, and prevent disruptions to investment flows during the initial operational phase.
Under existing regulations, investors and VIFC members are generally required to maintain accounts at licensed member banks or credit institutions operating within the centre.
The SBV said that this requirement would help authorities identify and monitor cash flows and support the management and supervision of capital entering and leaving the centre.
However, with no member bank yet licensed and operational, temporary account arrangements were considered necessary to ensure that investment activities could proceed without interruption.
The SBV is also proposing changes to international credit rating requirements for foreign banks seeking to establish wholly foreign-owned commercial banks or branches at the IFC.
Current regulations require applicants to have a credit rating of at least AA- from Standard & Poor's or Fitch Ratings, or Aa3 from Moody's.

However, investors and the VIFC's executive authorities have said these thresholds are too stringent, potentially preventing some major, financially sound international banks interested in joining the centre from meeting the licensing requirements.

The draft proposes recognising ratings from other international credit rating agencies registered or endorsed by the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), or authorised to issue credit ratings in G7 countries, provided the rating is at least AA.
The proposal is expected to broaden the pool of eligible international financial institutions and make the VIFC more attractive to foreign investors.
The SBV said several banks might already meet the existing licensing requirements and be ready to submit applications.

However, more time was needed to review applications and complete approval procedures while banks would also need time to prepare information technology systems, recruit personnel and establish governance structures before officially launching operations.
Nine Vietnamese banks have recently approved or begun seeking shareholder approval to establish subsidiary banks at the VIFC.
They include Vietcombank, MB, Techcombank, HDBank, MSB, SHB, TPBank, LPBank and Nam A Bank. - VNS
